questions.stem: These photographs show bluish discoloration of the fingers and toes in a patient with a congenital heart defect. What underlying pathophysiology produces this finding?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Left-to-right shunting increasing pulmonary blood flow

explanation.summary: Central cyanosis in congenital heart disease reflects a right-to-left shunt, which delivers deoxygenated blood directly to the systemic circulation, raising deoxyhemoglobin above roughly 5 g/dL and producing the bluish skin and nail discoloration.
explanation.whyCorrect: Central cyanosis in congenital heart disease reflects a right-to-left shunt, which delivers deoxygenated blood directly to the systemic circulation, raising deoxyhemoglobin above roughly 5 g/dL and producing the bluish skin and nail discoloration.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Arterial thrombotic occlusion causes focal ischemia of one limb or digit, not symmetric bluish discoloration of the fingers and toes in congenital heart disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Left-to-right shunting sends oxygenated blood back to the lungs and is acyanotic until Eisenmenger reversal develops.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Carbon monoxide poisoning produces normal or cherry-red skin color, not cyanosis, because carboxyhemoglobin is not blue.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Anemia causes pallor, and severe anemia actually makes cyanosis harder to see because less deoxyhemoglobin is present.

questions.stem: Compared with the normal heart on the left, the right panel shows a long-standing ventricular septal defect. The inset vessel demonstrates a thickened tunica media and narrowed lumen. What process does this illustrate?

choices.label: B

choices.label: C
choices.text: Systemic hypertension from renal artery stenosis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Aortic dissection propagating through the media

choices.label: E

explanation.summary: Chronic left-to-right shunting raises pulmonary blood flow and pressure, driving medial hypertrophy and luminal narrowing of pulmonary arteries; the resulting pulmonary hypertension increases right ventricular afterload and causes RV hypertrophy (potentially leading to Eisenmenger shunt reversal).

whyWrongByChoice.B: Deep venous thrombosis involves clot in a peripheral vein, not medial hypertrophy of an artery from shunt flow.

questions.stem: The right-hand diagram shows a persistent connection between the aorta and pulmonary artery after birth. Which fetal structure has failed to close to produce this defect?

explanation.whyCorrect: A patent ductus arteriosus results when the fetal ductus arteriosus (which normally shunts blood from the pulmonary artery to the aorta in utero) fails to close after birth, leaving an aorta-to-pulmonary artery connection.

whyWrongByChoice.D: The coronary sinus drains cardiac veins into the right atrium and is a permanent structure, not a fetal shunt.

questions.stem: In the patent ductus arteriosus shown at right, blood flows through the abnormal connection between the aorta and the pulmonary artery. In which direction does blood shunt through this connection after birth?

choices.label: C
choices.text: From left ventricle to right ventricle

choices.label: D
choices.text: From right atrium to left atrium

choices.label: E
choices.text: There is no net flow because pressures are equal

explanation.summary: Because systemic (aortic) pressure normally exceeds pulmonary pressure, a patent ductus arteriosus produces a left-to-right shunt from the aorta into the pulmonary artery, increasing pulmonary blood flow.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because systemic (aortic) pressure normally exceeds pulmonary pressure, a patent ductus arteriosus produces a left-to-right shunt from the aorta into the pulmonary artery, increasing pulmonary blood flow.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Right-to-left ductal flow occurs only if pulmonary pressure exceeds systemic pressure, as in Eisenmenger syndrome or persistent pulmonary hypertension.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Flow from the left to the right ventricle requires a ventricular septal defect, not a ductal connection between the great vessels.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Flow between the atria occurs through an atrial septal defect or foramen ovale, not the ductus arteriosus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Aortic pressure exceeds pulmonary pressure throughout the cycle after birth, so there is continuous net flow.

choices.text: Higher pressure on the left side drives blood from left to right

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gravity directs blood downward through the ventricular defect

explanation.whyCorrect: Left-sided chambers operate at higher pressure than the corresponding right-sided chambers, so uncomplicated septal defects initially shunt oxygenated blood left-to-right, increasing pulmonary flow and right heart volume.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Gravity does not determine intracardiac flow; pressure gradients between chambers drive shunting.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Oxygen content does not pull blood; the shunt direction is determined by pressure differences.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Valve incompetence produces regurgitation within one side, not flow across a septal defect, and the arrows show left-to-right flow.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Uncomplicated defects have a pressure difference, so flow is predominantly unidirectional left-to-right rather than balanced.

questions.stem: Comparing the fetal heart (left) with the newborn heart (right), what triggers the functional closure of the foramen ovale at birth?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A sudden fall in systemic arterial oxygen tension

choices.label: C
choices.text: A drop in left ventricular contractility after delivery

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased prostaglandin production by the placenta

choices.label: E
choices.text: Constriction of the umbilical vein at birth

explanation.summary: With the first breaths, pulmonary vascular resistance falls and pulmonary venous return rises, increasing left atrial pressure above right atrial pressure; this pressure reversal presses the septum primum against the septum secundum, functionally closing the foramen ovale.
explanation.whyCorrect: With the first breaths, pulmonary vascular resistance falls and pulmonary venous return rises, increasing left atrial pressure above right atrial pressure; this pressure reversal presses the septum primum against the septum secundum, functionally closing the foramen ovale.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Systemic oxygen tension rises, not falls, after birth, and it drives ductus closure rather than foramen ovale closure.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Left ventricular contractility does not fall after delivery, and it does not move the septal flap.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Placental prostaglandins keep the ductus open; their loss at birth helps close the ductus, not the foramen ovale.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Umbilical vein constriction lowers inferior vena cava return and right atrial pressure, which contributes, but the closing force is the rise in left atrial pressure.

questions.stem: These three schematics classify coarctation of the aorta by its position relative to the ductus arteriosus. The form that typically presents in the neonatal period with lower-body cyanosis and collapse when the ductus closes is which type?

whyWrongByChoice.C: Postductal coarctation develops collaterals and usually presents later with arm hypertension and weak femoral pulses, not in neonatal collapse.

explanation.summary: Cyanosis of the digits appears when the absolute amount of deoxygenated (reduced) hemoglobin in the blood rises, giving skin and mucosa a bluish color; in right-to-left shunts this reflects poorly oxygenated blood reaching the systemic circulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cyanosis of the digits appears when the absolute amount of deoxygenated (reduced) hemoglobin in the blood rises, giving skin and mucosa a bluish color; in right-to-left shunts this reflects poorly oxygenated blood reaching the systemic circulation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bilirubin deposition causes jaundice, a yellow discoloration of skin and sclerae, not bluish digits.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Methemoglobinemia can cause slate-gray cyanosis, but it reflects abnormal ferric hemoglobin, not the shunt-related rise in deoxyhemoglobin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Iron overload causes a bronze or gray skin pigmentation, as in hemochromatosis, not dusky bluish digits.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Carboxyhemoglobin is cherry red and does not produce a bluish color, even though it impairs oxygen delivery.

questions.stem: This heart shows four features: pulmonary valve stenosis, an overriding aorta, a ventricular septal defect, and an enlarged (hypertrophied) right ventricle. What is the diagnosis?

explanation.summary: The tetrad of pulmonary stenosis, overriding aorta, ventricular septal defect, and right ventricular hypertrophy defines Tetralogy of Fallot, the most common cyanotic congenital heart disease of childhood.
explanation.whyCorrect: The tetrad of pulmonary stenosis, overriding aorta, ventricular septal defect, and right ventricular hypertrophy defines Tetralogy of Fallot, the most common cyanotic congenital heart disease of childhood.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tricuspid atresia lacks a tricuspid valve and has a hypoplastic right ventricle, not an overriding aorta with RV hypertrophy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Transposition has the aorta arising from the RV and pulmonary artery from the LV, without the overriding aorta or classic tetrad.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Truncus arteriosus has a single great vessel over a VSD, not separate aorta and stenotic pulmonary valve.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Total anomalous pulmonary venous return is an abnormal venous connection to the right heart, without pulmonary stenosis or overriding aorta.

questions.stem: This infant illustration shows bluish discoloration of the lips, hands, and feet. What does this appearance most likely indicate?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Normal newborn acrocyanosis that resolves within hours

choices.label: D
choices.text: Central cyanosis from a right-to-left cardiac shunt

choices.label: E
choices.text: Jaundice from hemolytic disease of the newborn

explanation.summary: Bluish discoloration involving the lips and trunk (not just the extremities) indicates central cyanosis, seen when a right-to-left shunt delivers deoxygenated blood to the systemic circulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bluish discoloration involving the lips and trunk (not just the extremities) indicates central cyanosis, seen when a right-to-left shunt delivers deoxygenated blood to the systemic circulation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Birth-trauma bruising is localized to the presenting part, not symmetric blue lips, hands, and feet.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Anemia causes pallor, a white appearance, rather than bluish discoloration.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Acrocyanosis affects only the hands and feet; blue lips indicate central cyanosis, which is never normal.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Jaundice produces yellow skin and sclerae, not bluish lips and extremities.

questions.stem: This patient's fingertips appear dusky and bulbous. Chronic hypoxemia from a cyanotic heart defect classically produces which finger finding?

explanation.summary: Long-standing hypoxemia stimulates soft-tissue proliferation at the nail beds, producing the bulbous fingertips and increased nail curvature known as digital clubbing.
explanation.whyCorrect: Long-standing hypoxemia stimulates soft-tissue proliferation at the nail beds, producing the bulbous fingertips and increased nail curvature known as digital clubbing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Leukonychia is white discoloration of the nails, as in hypoalbuminemia or trauma, not bulbous fingertips.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Splinter hemorrhages are linear red-brown streaks under the nail, associated with endocarditis rather than chronic hypoxemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Koilonychia is a thin, concave nail of iron deficiency, the opposite of the convex, bulbous clubbed nail.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Beau's lines are transverse grooves from temporary nail growth arrest during systemic illness.

questions.stem: In this diagram the aorta carries purple 'mixed blood' because blood crosses the labeled shunts. What is the physiologic consequence of this mixing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reduced pulmonary blood flow with normal systemic oxygenation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Complete separation of the pulmonary and systemic circulations

choices.label: C
choices.text: Isolated left ventricular hypertrophy without cyanosis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Left-to-right shunting causing pulmonary overcirculation only

choices.label: E
choices.text: Systemic delivery of partially deoxygenated blood

explanation.summary: When oxygen-poor and oxygen-rich blood mix through connections such as a patent ductus arteriosus and foramen ovale, the aorta ejects blood of intermediate oxygen content to the body, causing cyanosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: When oxygen-poor and oxygen-rich blood mix through connections such as a patent ductus arteriosus and foramen ovale, the aorta ejects blood of intermediate oxygen content to the body, causing cyanosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mixing oxygen-poor blood into the aorta lowers systemic oxygenation, so oxygenation cannot be normal.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The shunts connect the two circulations; complete separation would mean no mixing at all.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Isolated LV hypertrophy without cyanosis describes pressure overload such as aortic stenosis, not mixed blood in the aorta.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pure left-to-right shunting keeps systemic blood fully oxygenated, whereas this aorta carries mixed blood.

questions.stem: In the anomaly on the right, all pulmonary venous blood returns to the right atrium. Why is the labeled atrial septal defect essential for the infant to survive?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It equalizes pressures to reverse the direction of shunting

choices.label: B
choices.text: It allows deoxygenated blood to bypass stenotic lungs

choices.label: C
choices.text: It reflexively closes the ductus arteriosus

choices.label: D
choices.text: It decompresses the left ventricle to prevent failure

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is the only route for oxygenated blood to reach the systemic circulation

explanation.summary: When pulmonary veins connect anomalously to the systemic venous system, all blood collects in the right atrium; a right-to-left shunt across an atrial septal defect is the only way oxygenated blood can pass to the left heart and body.
explanation.whyCorrect: When pulmonary veins connect anomalously to the systemic venous system, all blood collects in the right atrium; a right-to-left shunt across an atrial septal defect is the only way oxygenated blood can pass to the left heart and body.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The atrial defect does not reverse shunting; it permits obligatory right-to-left flow from the overloaded right atrium.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The lungs are not stenotic, and the problem is getting already oxygenated pulmonary venous blood to the left heart, not bypassing the lungs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An atrial septal defect has no reflex effect on the ductus arteriosus, which closes with rising oxygen and falling prostaglandins.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The left ventricle is underfilled in this anomaly, so it needs inflow rather than decompression.
